p: The O2 is one of the busiest entertainment venues in the world, hosting big-name concerts, comedy shows and sporting events throughout the year. When you've got tickets for a show, the hours before the doors open can drag if you've not planned anything. A games bar inside the dome gives you a perfect way to fill that gap, with drinks, food and a few competitive rounds.

The easiest way to arrive is on the Jubilee line to North Greenwich, which drops you right outside. You can also take the Uber Boat by Thames Clippers river service, which stops at the O2 pier, or the cable car across the river from the Royal Docks. If you're driving, there's parking on site, but it gets very busy on event nights.

For the best experience, plan your timings carefully. Big shows bring huge crowds, so allow extra time to get in and settle down, and book your game slot well ahead. Make sure you know when the doors open for your show, and give yourselves plenty of time to finish up and head to your seats without rushing.

If you've got the whole day free, the Greenwich Peninsula has a riverside walk with views of Canary Wharf, and the Thames Barrier is a short way downriver. And Greenwich town centre, with its market and maritime history, is just a short bus or boat ride away.
